# Results {#sec-results}

## Where affordability is strained

Affordability salary has clear geographic structure before any modeling. The counties where income stretches furthest are not the counties where income is highest, which is the gap the price adjustment is built to close.

<!-- fig-affordmap. EXISTS poster Fig 4. Rebuild on 848 panel. -->

     Cut one of the two maps? -->

## Task groups and affordability

The panel regression returns a negative association between non-routine manual work and affordability salary that holds after controls. A one percentage point shift toward non-routine manual work, and away from the non-routine cognitive reference, is associated with roughly \$1,041 less in affordability salary. Routine cognitive and routine manual follow at \$858 and \$701. @fig-coefplot shows each coefficient with its confidence interval.

<!-- fig-coefplot. NEW. Coefficient plot, task group on y, association with affordability
     salary on x, non-routine cognitive reference. Priority. -->

The associations survive the addition of poverty rate and the other baseline controls, so the task groups are not standing in for poverty. @fig-coefcompare puts the coefficients before and after controls side by side.

<!-- fig-coefcompare. NEW. Paired forest plot, each task group before and after adding
     poverty and baseline controls. -->

## Beyond a straight line

The linear specification does not fit equally well across the range. Residuals curve away from zero at both ends and fan outward, and the model underpredicts the least and most affordable counties by roughly \$8,000 to \$9,000 at each tail. @fig-binned shows the same structure directly: binned means of affordability salary across the range of routine cognitive work rise and then fall rather than tracking a straight line.

## What the models weigh

Task groups carry real explanatory weight alongside poverty rate rather than substituting for it, and the ordering is consistent across the regression and the random forest. Poverty rate is the single largest contributor in the forest, which is why the coefficient comparison above matters: it shows the task group associations persist once poverty is in the model.

## Stability over time

A county's task composition moves very little across the fifteen year panel. Rank correlations between the first and last observed years run from 0.451 to 0.865 across the four groups, so counties hold their relative position. This matters for interpretation. Because composition is close to a fixed characteristic of place, the affordability differences associated with it do not fade, and they are not something residents can be expected to move out from under.

<!-- fig-stability. NEW. Stacked area, year on x, task group share on y, four bands. -->

## Robustness

Restricting the panel to 2010 onward, which removes the occupation coding change described in @sec-data, leaves the main associations intact. Splitting further into pre pandemic and post pandemic windows gives the same picture: non-routine manual is stable within 2.6 percent across eras, routine manual within 6.6 percent, routine cognitive within 12.5 percent, and the ordering of the three is identical in every window.
